resultados.explicacion: Estar de gira means being on tour, as bands and performers are.
Me he enterado por la prensa means I learnt about it from the newspapers.
Me he quedado sin batería means the battery has run out or gone flat.
No llego a fin de mes means I don't have enough money to last the month.
No conseguimos ponernos de acuerdo means we failed to reach an agreement.
Por casualidad means by chance, so it happened unexpectedly.
Sequía means drought, a long period without rain, unlike floods.
Una ola de calor is a period of very hot weather, not a wave in the sea.
Recaudan dinero para una ONG means they collect money for a charity.
Suelta is the command form of soltar, which means to let go of.
Un recuerdo means a keepsake or memento that reminds you of someone.
Llevan cinco años viviendo juntos uses llevar for a period still continuing now.
Póngame is a polite shop request, and judías verdes are green beans.
Salimos de copas means we went out for drinks, usually to bars.
Me he equivocado de aula means I made a mistake and went to the wrong room.
Se requiere means is required, and disponibilidad means availability.
Aficionado al bricolaje means keen on DIY, the hobby of home repairs.
Soleado means sunny, and el piso is the flat.
Hemos estado en un atasco: estar means to be, and atasco means traffic jam.
El casco antiguo means the old part of a town, and it is not a helmet.
Me atendieron means they served or dealt with me, and amabilidad means kindness.
Entre in a sum means divided by, so seis entre dos means six divided by two.
Hay que cortar el césped means the grass must be cut, since césped means lawn.
Incluso means even, so the sentence says even the bosses prefer working at home.
O sea means in other words, used to restate or explain what was said.
Quieras o no means whether you want it or not, with the subjunctive.
No sea que llueva means in case it rains, as a precaution.
Llegó a insultarme means he reached the point of insulting me.
Una vez terminada la reunión means once the meeting was finished, then we left.
La cocina no es lo mío means cooking is not my thing or my strength.
Por lo visto means apparently, from what people seem to say or see.
Por poco me caigo means I almost fell, so I did not actually fall.
Por pura casualidad means purely by chance, not through an agreed coincidence.
Ambos means both, referring to two people or things.
La frente means forehead, and una cicatriz is a scar.
Eso ya lo sabía means I already knew that, with eso as the thing known.
Le guste o no means whether he likes it or not, using the subjunctive.
¿Me alcanzas…? asks you to pass or hand me something within reach.
No tengo por qué means I have no reason to, so I don't have to.
Salvo que sea una urgencia means unless it is an emergency.
